pr_title: QL: Combine multiple equal queries into In
pr_body:
Some queries can have an excessive number of OR clauses on the same
field (typically by being generated). This can lead to large query
requests that can cause SO errors.
This PR tries to address this pattern by combining the equals into an
In expression which in turn gets compressed into a terms query vs one
term query per entry.

Fix #62804
Fix #46477
pr_comments: The tests keep on failing due to #65419 - depending on the expression, either the rule gets triggered constantly or the unit test fails. I'll merge this after the other PR to account for the change.

issue_context.title: QL: Improve disjunction translations on the same field
issue_context.body:
Queries with a lot of `OR` clauses on the same field, end up being translated to individual bool clauses for every single expression. While correct this can result in very large, non-optimal requests which in turn can lead to other problems (see #46477).
QL can optimize this scenario away so the multiple bool queries are translated into a terms one,
comments: This is a task for the far future, considering https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/61596#discussion_r490123586 right? Or limited to SQL for the moment.
Correct, this works if/when dealing with exact equals. Case insensitive equals, the default currently in EQL, breaks this so at least for the moment, this would work only in SQL.

review_comments: QQ: I guess the `IN` could contain non foldable expressions? Wouldn't a similar check be useful for IN's elements?
`In` requires all values to be foldable and checks this inside its `resolveType`. Hence why any `In` produced will only have foldable expressions.
